properties.name: A684 Hawes–Sedbergh
properties.reason: Main Dales A-road but narrow and twisty in places with villages, stone walls and farm traffic. Penfold is suitable; expect slower progress than the road class suggests.

properties.name: B6255 Ingleton–Hawes
properties.reason: Scenic B-road through limestone country with bends and exposed sections. Normally a comfortable Penfold route, but livestock and tourist traffic can slow progress.

properties.name: B6160 Wharfedale road
properties.reason: Narrow Dales B-road through villages and stone-walled sections. Penfold fits, but meeting traffic and cyclists make a cautious pace sensible.

properties.name: Coverdale road
properties.reason: Long narrow minor-road valley route with stone walls, blind bends and limited passing. Penfold can use it, but this should be an intentional route rather than a shortcut.

properties.name: Malham Tarn road
properties.reason: Narrow upland access with stone walls and tourist traffic. Penfold is physically suitable, but meeting vehicles may require reversing to passing opportunities.

properties.name: A65 Skipton–Kendal
properties.reason: Major trunk-style route along the southern/western edge of the Dales. Default green for Penfold and the sensible alternative to minor cross-Dales lanes.
properties.evidence: National Park travel guidance + road class

properties.name: A59 Skipton–Harrogate corridor
properties.reason: Major access route bordering the Dales, suitable for commercial traffic and straightforward for Penfold.
properties.evidence: National Park travel guidance + road class

properties.name: A623 Peak District corridor
properties.reason: Main cross-Peak A-road used by regular through traffic. Default suitable for Penfold except temporary closures or signed restrictions.

properties.name: A6 Bakewell–Buxton
properties.reason: Primary Peak District corridor, regularly used by buses and HGVs. Default green for Penfold.

properties.name: A515 Ashbourne–Buxton
properties.reason: Main north-south A-road across the southern Peak District. Suitable for Penfold and preferable to minor-lane shortcuts.

properties.name: B6049 Monsal Head–Tideswell
properties.reason: Bendy rural B-road with narrow sections and tourist traffic. Penfold is suitable but take care through villages and around cyclists.

properties.name: Edale valley road
properties.reason: Narrow valley access with parked cars, walkers and limited passing. Penfold fits, but busy periods make reversing and careful positioning likely.

properties.name: A57 Sheffield–Glossop
properties.reason: Main cross-Peak route via Snake Pass; suitable for Penfold, but steep bends, weather and closures justify yellow rather than blanket green.

properties.name: Washgate green lane
properties.reason: Peak District National Park lists Washgate under a Traffic Regulation Order prohibiting mechanically propelled vehicles. Treat as a hard no for Penfold.

properties.name: Wetton Hills green lane
properties.reason: Peak District National Park lists Wetton Hills under a permanent prohibition of mechanically propelled vehicles. Not a Penfold route.

properties.name: B3212 Moretonhampstead–Princetown
properties.reason: One of Dartmoor's main moorland roads. It is exposed and bendy but generally appropriate for campervans; livestock and weather are the main issues.
properties.evidence: National Park motorhome guidance + road class

properties.name: B3357 Two Bridges–Tavistock
properties.reason: Open moorland B-road with bends and livestock. Penfold is suitable, though Dartmoor warns that some minor roads and small bridges are unsuitable for motorhomes.
properties.evidence: National Park motorhome guidance + road class

properties.name: B3212 Yelverton–Princetown
properties.reason: Main moorland approach to Princetown. Generally suitable for Penfold, with exposed weather and livestock more significant than vehicle dimensions.
properties.evidence: National Park motorhome guidance + road class

properties.name: Hexworthy–Dartmeet minor road
properties.reason: Narrow moorland road with stone walls, bridges and limited passing. Dartmoor specifically warns that some roads and small bridges are off limits to motorhomes; this is a cautious Penfold route.
properties.evidence: National Park motorhome guidance + road geometry

properties.name: A386 Tavistock–Okehampton
properties.reason: Main western Dartmoor corridor, substantially easier than minor moorland roads and a sensible Penfold route.

properties.name: A39 Minehead–Lynton
properties.reason: Main Exmoor coastal route with steep and twisty sections including Countisbury. Penfold is suitable, but gradients and bends merit care.

properties.name: B3223 Simonsbath–Exford
properties.reason: Narrow moorland B-road but generally manageable for Penfold. Exmoor specialises in narrow lanes, so expect livestock and limited passing.

properties.name: Malmsmead–Oareford road
properties.reason: Exmoor National Park specifically calls for particular care on the narrow road between Malmsmead and Oareford. Penfold fits, but farm access and tight lanes make this deliberate-route territory.

properties.name: Porlock Vale minor lanes
properties.reason: Exmoor National Park business guidance notes that local narrow lanes can be unsuitable for caravans and motorhomes. Penfold is smaller, but route selection matters around the vale.

properties.name: A470 Brecon–Merthyr
properties.reason: Major north-south trunk route across Bannau Brycheiniog. Straightforward for Penfold and the sensible alternative to minor mountain roads.

properties.name: A40 Brecon–Abergavenny
properties.reason: Principal east-west route through the eastern Brecon Beacons area, routinely used by commercial traffic and suitable for Penfold.

properties.name: A487 Machynlleth–Aberystwyth
properties.reason: Primary west-Wales corridor. Bendy in places but built for through traffic and a sensible Penfold route.

properties.name: A494 Dolgellau–Bala
properties.reason: Main route between Dolgellau and Bala and a much easier Penfold choice than Bwlch y Groes or tiny mountain alternatives.

properties.name: B4407 Ffestiniog–Ysbyty Ifan
properties.reason: Rural cross-country B-road with narrow sections. Penfold is suitable but expect bends, livestock and occasional constrained passing.

properties.name: A82 Loch Ness corridor
properties.reason: Major trunk route along Loch Ness, routinely used by coaches and HGVs. Default green for Penfold despite bends and tourist traffic.

properties.name: A887 Invermoriston–A87
properties.reason: Strategic link from the A82 toward Skye, suitable for normal commercial traffic and straightforward for Penfold.

properties.name: A890 Strathcarron corridor
properties.reason: Main west-coast link with some narrower Highland sections. Penfold is appropriate; weather and passing-place behaviour matter more than dimensions.

properties.name: A835 Ullapool–Ledmore
properties.reason: Main strategic road north from Ullapool and the sensible Penfold route before choosing any smaller Assynt deviations.

properties.name: A838 Lairg–Durness
properties.reason: Long remote route with extensive single-track sections. Penfold is an appropriate size, but NC500 guidance stresses reversing ability and passing-place discipline.
